subject: Request: one-off islanded deployment constraints + limited audit window (SafeHarbor Health)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, legal-team@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Request: islanded deployment constraints + limited audit window (SafeHarbor Health)

Team —

Following the final commercial review with SafeHarbor Health, procurement has returned our MAA with three non-standard asks that touch infra, security and commercial:

1) Islanded (air-gapped/VPC) deployment model: customer requires a logically isolated VPC in our dedicated offering and strict egress controls.
2) Audit window: they will require an on-site auditor with a "one business week" window annually, but only for a designated engineering host and limited to network & access logs.
3) Pricing/credits: they expect a 20% committed discount for a 36-month reserved capacity deal and an onboarding credit for an 8-week pilot.

I've attached their redlines (SafeHarbor_MAA_redlines.pdf) and a proposed topology they sent (island_deploy_diagram.png). Key constraints: they will not accept any offsite log export for audit evidence; they insist on physical presence for the auditor and a locked-down ephemeral VM to host the reviewer.

Commercial note: this is an expansion sale with material ARR and strategic healthcare reference potential. Marcus — leaning on you for recommendation on discount cap and whether deal desk should escalate pricing.

Prioym / Grace — can you confirm whether we can support the narrow audit scope and on-site auditor constraints without exposing platform IP / multi-tenant risk? Also is KMS escrow an option here?

Asking for an exec exception/approval on two fronts: (A) approve a one-time 20% discount + onboarding credit OR provide counter (we should not exceed 15% without exec OK), and (B) approve a constrained audit acceptance model (on-site, 1-week window, read-only access to a restricted evidence VM) with legal to add indemnities/limitations.

I captured the timeline: customer wants contract signed by 2027-07-07 to align with their quarter close.

Next steps: Marcus to advise pricing, infra & security to confirm feasibility, legal to prepare carveback language. If this needs exec signoff, looping Laura.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Request: islanded deployment constraints + limited audit window (SafeHarbor Health)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the write-up and attachments. Quick take:

- Commercial: 36-month term + reserved capacity with pilot makes this attractive. Standard deal desk policy caps strategic discounts at 15% for renewals/expansions without C-suite approval. 20% would need Laura's signoff. The onboarding credit should be limited (we can offer up to $25k one-time credit tied to milestones).

- Risk/ops: the on-site audit ask + no offsite log export increases operational load and legal risk. If infra can isolate a single customer environment (true physical/VM isolation with separate keys) and legal can negotiate a narrow proof-of-compliance scope, I'm supportive of pursuing.

Action: Laura — can we greenlight up to 18% if we attach a clawback clause and require SOC2 plus a quarterly attestation for the first year? Otherwise 15% firm.

I'll hold the customer cadence to avoid losing momentum; Kimberly — can you please push the DocuSign link but mark it "pending exec approval" in the email thread?

-Marcus

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: islanded deployment constraints + limited audit window (SafeHarbor Health)

On Thu, Jun 30, 2027 at 01:04 PM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kimberly —
>
> Thanks for the write-up and attachments. Quick take: ...

Folks — technical reality: we can deliver a logically islanded VPC in Dedicated and provide a restricted "evidence VM" but there are trade-offs:

- True physical air-gap is not feasible for multi-tenant Dedicated; we can provide strong network segmentation, customer-dedicated nodes & dedicated KMS keys (bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed customer keys).
- On-site auditor access: we can spin up a locked read-only VM within the customer's dedicated subnet and produce the requested network/access logs. However, logs are partially dependent on retention policies and our observability stack; per-customer retention extension is possible but incurs storage/costs we need to bill or include in the deal.
- We cannot allow an auditor to export raw platform logs that may include multi-tenant metadata. We can provide filtered, redacted extracts and a time-boxed remote session to view evidence on the ephemeral VM.

Recommendations:
1) Approve a constrained audit mode: on-site auditor with supervised access to a read-only evidence VM, no raw log exports, and a documented redaction process.
2) Require customer to accept an indemnity clause restricting the scope of the audit to the customer's environment only.
3) Approve KMS separation and BYOK if they require exclusive control of keys.

Operational asks if approved: 2-week lead time for provisioning the dedicated environment, and a one-time implementation fee (suggest $30k) to cover segregation and extended retention.

I'll draft a short technical appendix for legal to include in the MAA describing what auditors can/cannot see.

—Priyom

Priyom Das
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: islanded deployment constraints + limited audit window (SafeHarbor Health)

Kimberly / Marcus / Priyom —

After reviewing the commercial and technical notes, I approve an exception with the following binding conditions:

1) Discount: up to 15% standard; we can stretch to 18% only if Finance signs off on the ARR uplift model and a 12-month clawback is included if low utilization / early termination. No more than 18% under any circumstance.

2) Onboarding credit: cap at $25,000 and tied to a successful pilot milestones report (clear acceptance criteria).

3) Audit scope: approve the constrained audit mode described by Priyom (on-site, supervised, read-only evidence VM). Legal must insert a narrow audit appendix that: specifies exact artifacts, prohibits raw platform metadata export, includes redaction rules, and requires the auditor to sign an NDA and agreement limiting reproduction.

4) KMS & Keys: BYOK allowed if customer provides KMS and we verify integration; otherwise provide dedicated-key option with key rotation policy.

5) Fees: implement a one-time segregation fee ($30k) to be invoiced on contract signature; cost must be modeled into the deal economics.

6) Compliance prerequisites: customer must be SOC2 Type II at signing or provide an attestation and agree to quarterly compliance check-ins for the first year.

7) Review & sunset: this exception is timebound — review after 12 months. Any future requests that expand access or audit scope will require C-level approval.

Marcus / Kimberly: please communicate these items to SafeHarbor and have legal prepare a redlined MAA with the audit appendix and the DocuSign envelope marked "pending exec conditions". Legal, please include the clawback language and proof-of-utilization milestones.

If the customer accepts, Finance will approve the stretched 18% provided the ARR and clawback align.

Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
